name: Concept E: Po-210 direct-charge ion drive
description: Exotic and speculative (TRL 2–3). Matches analysis/ideas_calc.py: 0.4 kg Po-210 at 144 W/g supplies 57.6 kW thermal initially, with 138.376 day half-life. Assumed 30% direct-charge conversion and 70% ion-thruster efficiency yield 2.086e11 J of total jet energy, 323 km/s exhaust, and 316.792 km/s rocket delta-v from 6.4 kg wet / 2.4 kg dry. A radial outward equivalent impulse from a circular 1 AU orbit gives solar v∞ 315.388 km/s. All future exponential decay energy is integrated at constant Isp and applied at the start; the months-long powered path, changing gravity, steering, thermal management and Earth escape are not propagated. The 2.4 kg dry mass includes the isotope and hardware. Showstopper: 0.4 kg Po-210 is about four times world output and loses about 0.5% of its power per day; 30% conversion efficiency is assumed versus a few percent demonstrated.

events.notes: Constant 323 km/s xenon exhaust (~71 kV). Integrate all future decay energy (an infinite-time upper bound) and apply 316.792 km/s radially outward at launch, retaining the initial tangential orbital velocity. No finite-thrust propagation: the preview shows the post-impulse coast, not the actual powered mission.
